criteria.text: The allergen(s) to which the patient is allergic must be clinically relevant.
criteria.source_quote: The allergen(s) to which the patient is allergic must be clinically relevant
criteria.if_missing: Is the identified allergen documented as clinically relevant to the patient's history/exposure?

criteria.text: Trial of avoidance measures has failed or there is unavoidable exposure to allergy triggers identified in allergy testing.
criteria.source_quote: Trial of avoidance measures has failed or there is unavoidable exposure to allergy triggers identified in allergy testing
criteria.if_missing: Has avoidance been tried and failed, or is there documented unavoidable exposure to the identified allergen?
criteria.short: No failed avoidance trial or unavoidable exposure documented

criteria.text: The condition being treated must be one of the covered indications (allergic rhinitis, allergic conjunctivitis, allergic asthma, dust mite atopic dermatitis, or stinging insect hypersensitivity).
criteria.source_quote: Conditions for which immunotherapy will be considered medically reasonable and necessary include:
criteria.if_missing: What is the patient's diagnosis being treated with immunotherapy?

criteria.text: Allergen immunotherapy is not medically necessary for food hypersensitivity, cockroach hypersensitivity, or urticaria/angioedema.
criteria.source_quote:
Allergen immunotherapy is not considered medically reasonable and necessary for :

Food hypersensitivity 1,12-14

Cockroach hypersensitivity 1

Urticaria and/or angioedema
criteria.if_missing: What is the patient's diagnosis being treated with immunotherapy?
criteria.short: Diagnosis is an excluded indication (food, cockroach, urticaria/angioedema)

criteria.text: Provocation-neutralization therapy is not medically necessary.
Low-dose subcutaneous therapy based on the Rinkel method is not medically necessary.
criteria.source_quote: Low-dose subcutaneous therapy based on the Rinkel method 6,12,13
criteria.if_missing: Is the therapy a low-dose subcutaneous Rinkel-method protocol?
criteria.short: Rinkel method low-dose subcutaneous therapy used

criteria.text: Therapy formulations such as allergoids or adjuvants are not medically necessary.
criteria.source_quote: Therapy formulations, such as allergoids or adjuvants 1
criteria.if_missing: Does the formulation include allergoids or adjuvants?

criteria.text: Certain routes of administration (oral/sublingual for food, epicutaneous, intralymphatic, intranasal, sublingual) are not medically necessary.
criteria.source_quote:
The following routes of administration 6,12,13 :

Oral or sublingual for food immunotherapy

Epicutaneous immunotherapy

Intralymphatic immunotherapy

Intranasal immunotherapy

Sublingual Immunotherapy
criteria.if_missing: What route of administration is used for the immunotherapy?

criteria.text: Immunotherapy for Hymenoptera venom sensitivity using whole-body extracts is not medically necessary, except for fire ant extracts.
criteria.source_quote: Immunotherapy for Hymenoptera venom sensitivity using whole-body extracts, with the exception of fire ant extracts
criteria.if_missing: Is the venom immunotherapy using a whole-body extract other than fire ant?

criteria.text: Patients should not have substantial comorbid conditions that could increase immunotherapy risk.
criteria.source_quote: Patients should not have substantial comorbid conditions that could increase immunotherapy risk
criteria.if_missing: Does the patient have substantial comorbid conditions (e.g., severe uncontrolled asthma, significant cardiovascular disease) that increase immunotherapy risk?

criteria.text: Patients on beta-blockers and/or ACE inhibitors must have an individualized risk versus benefit assessment prior to receiving inhalant or venom allergen immunotherapy.
criteria.source_quote: Patients on beta-blockers and/or angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitor medications must have individualized assessments of risk versus benefit prior to receiving inhalant or venom allergen immunotherapy.
criteria.if_missing: If the patient is on a beta-blocker or ACE inhibitor, was an individualized risk/benefit assessment documented prior to immunotherapy?
criteria.short: No individualized risk/benefit assessment documented for beta-blocker/ACE inhibitor patient

criteria.text: Patients should be able to cooperate during therapy.
criteria.source_quote: Patients should be able to cooperate during therapy.
criteria.if_missing: Is the patient documented as able to cooperate during therapy?
criteria.short: Patient unable to cooperate during therapy

criteria.text: Services must be within the scope of practice of the provider's professional licensure and performed per state supervision requirements by appropriately trained providers.
criteria.source_quote: Services will be considered medically reasonable and necessary when all aspects of care are within the scope of practice of the provider's professional licensure, when performed according to the supervision requirements per state scope of practice laws, and when all procedures are performed by appropriately trained providers
criteria.if_missing: Was the immunotherapy administered within the provider's licensed scope of practice, per state supervision rules, by an appropriately trained provider?
criteria.short: Provider not within scope/trained/supervised per requirements

new_facts.label: Allergen identified is clinically relevant (correlates with patient history/exposure)
new_facts.ask: Does the documentation state that the identified allergen correlates with the patient's clinical history and likely exposure?

new_facts.label: Avoidance trial failed or unavoidable allergen exposure
new_facts.ask: Does the packet document a failed trial of avoidance measures, or unavoidable exposure to the allergen identified on testing?

new_facts.label: Diagnosis being treated with immunotherapy
new_facts.ask: What diagnosis is the immunotherapy intended to treat?

new_facts.label: Specific immunotherapy technique/protocol used
new_facts.ask: What specific immunotherapy technique or protocol is being used (e.g., standard subcutaneous, provocation-neutralization, Rinkel method)?

new_facts.label: Type of allergen formulation used
new_facts.ask: What formulation of allergen extract is being used (e.g., standard aqueous extract, allergoid, adjuvant-containing)?

new_facts.label: Route of administration for immunotherapy
new_facts.ask: What route of administration is used for the allergen immunotherapy?

new_facts.label: Type of venom extract used for Hymenoptera immunotherapy
new_facts.ask: If treating Hymenoptera venom sensitivity, what type of extract is used (whole-body extract vs. venom extract vs. fire ant extract)?

new_facts.label: Presence of substantial comorbid condition increasing immunotherapy risk
new_facts.ask: Does the patient have a substantial comorbid condition (e.g., severe uncontrolled asthma, significant cardiovascular disease) that increases immunotherapy risk?

new_facts.label: Patient is on beta-blocker or ACE inhibitor medication
new_facts.ask: Is the patient currently taking a beta-blocker and/or ACE inhibitor medication?

new_facts.label: Individualized risk/benefit assessment documented for beta-blocker/ACE inhibitor patient
new_facts.ask: Is there documentation of an individualized risk versus benefit assessment for this patient prior to immunotherapy given their beta-blocker/ACE inhibitor use?

new_facts.label: Patient able to cooperate during therapy
new_facts.ask: Does the packet document that the patient is able to cooperate during immunotherapy administration?

new_facts.label: Provider administering/supervising therapy is within scope of practice, per state supervision rules, and appropriately trained
new_facts.ask: Is the provider administering or supervising the immunotherapy appropriately licensed, trained, and compliant with state supervision requirements?

not_modeled.quote: Patients should wait at the physician's office/medical clinic for at least 30 minutes after the immunotherapy injection.
not_modeled.why: This is a setting/monitoring recommendation ('recommended'), not a strict coverage criterion tied to a single checkable pass/fail fact for medical necessity determination.

not_modeled.quote: Home administration of allergen immunotherapy should only be considered in rare and exceptional cases when the benefits of immunotherapy clearly outweigh the risks.
not_modeled.why: Requires subjective clinical judgment balancing benefits/risks in rare/exceptional cases; not a simple binary fact a packet reviewer can check.

not_modeled.quote: A presumption of failure can be made when, after 12-24 months of therapy, a person does not experience: A noticeable decrease of symptoms, An increase in tolerance to the offending allergen, and A reduction in medication usage.
not_modeled.why: This describes a clinical presumption of treatment failure for ongoing therapy review, not a prior-authorization initiation criterion, and requires longitudinal outcome data not well suited to a single fact check.

not_modeled.quote: For many patients, the recommended duration of allergen immunotherapy is 3-5 years.
not_modeled.why: This is a general duration recommendation, not a strict pass/fail coverage requirement.
